chunk_map.heading: What would have to be true for your team to switch?

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L4 'Your proposal is not competing with nothing.' is the nearest: 'proposal' has no antecedent in the file, but it is the trio's own subject (arc-earned spine vocabulary carve-out) and every other pronoun resolves in-chunk ('that' = the digest/spreadsheet/gut call; 'them' = the team). Harm (reader cannot resolve a referent) absent.
L4-6: no pointer to another file or slide by position; the only callback is within the chunk ('competing with that').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L4 'a way of doing the work you want agents to join' names no beat the reader did/saw; no 'the X you did' phrase. grep of 'you (did|saw|caught)' in body: none.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no live-demo or guess-before-reveal beat; the muted read of L4-6 is fully verbed prose

rules_evaluated.evidence: L4-6: two paragraphs carrying a self-contained claim (the proposal competes with the current way; ask what would have to be true). Not an orphan.

L1 header asks what must be true for the team to switch; L6 gives three answers (lands where they look, right first try, trusted person). Closest: the answers are 'small and specific' vs a header promising 'true' conditions; still a literal match.

L6 'Not *how do we get the team to adopt this?* but *what would have to be true for them to switch?*' is a single not-X-but-Y reframe, not the banned 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' triple; 'It lands... It is right...' are two legs then a different-subject third (no anaphora triple, no empty verb triplet); no superlatives, no number+retraction.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep of body for compendium/surface/firing/beat/mood/forcing function: none; vocabulary is plain ('digest', 'spreadsheet', 'proposal'). View greps CLEAN.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body has no bold at all (L4-6; italics only on the two question phrases). Budget <=1 bold; 0 is inside.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Slide file carried by an include line in the enclosing lecture, which composes into the deck; no phase-less prose section. Presence is by the slide-file include mechanism (transparent inlining); no render-layer dependency in this body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/slides/what-would-make-your-team-switch.md -> 'OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.' No hand-numbered headers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/slides/what-would-make-your-team-switch.md -> 'OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no in-body links (view signals has_urls false, no [T](path) in body)

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/slides/what-would-make-your-team-switch.md -> 'oversized: 0', limits 210 words / 6 bullets, 1 slide.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L1 header is a question, not a claim; closest to a violation. This is a lecture-register slide, but the claim requirement binds law/consolidation slides where the header IS the teaching; here the header poses the question the body answers (home slide carries the same question header). Not a law slide.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L6 'The answers come back small and specific.' is the nearest bullet to restating, but it frames the three concrete answers that follow, adding the shape of the answer set; no doctrine restatement, design commentary or kicker.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L1 header was retitled from the home slide to 'your team' (maintainer L10), and the body was rewritten for the trio's proposal in the same edit: L4 'Your proposal is not competing with nothing' answers the new header; no inherited home-slide bullets remain.

notes: Single-chunk slide file; rule 10 judged on the include mechanism, not a rendered deck.
